t.7.16.1: Having conquered his brother Dhanada, O Rāma, the lord of the Rākṣasas then went to Śaravaṇa, the birthplace of Mahāsena.
t.7.16.2: Then Daśagrīva beheld the golden reed-forest, enveloped in a net of rays, like a second sun.
t.7.16.3: Having reached a mountain, a certain delightful stretch of forest, he saw there, O Rāma, the Puṣpaka brought to a standstill in the sky.
t.7.16.4: Seeing the Puṣpaka brought to a standstill, the chariot that moved at will now made unable to move, the Rākṣasa, surrounded by those ministers of his, fell to pondering.
t.7.16.5: What is this, on account of which my Puṣpaka does not move on? Whose doing could this be, of someone standing on top of the mountain?
t.7.16.6: Then Mārīca, wise in understanding, said to Daśagrīva: "This is not without cause, O king, that this Puṣpaka does not move."
t.7.16.7: Then, approaching his side, the mighty Nandīśvara, attendant of Bhava, fearlessly spoke these words to the lord of the Rākṣasas.
t.7.16.8: Turn back, Daśagrīva! Śaṃkara is at play upon this mountain.
t.7.16.9: This mountain has been made inaccessible to Suparṇas, Nāgas and Yakṣas, to Daityas, Dānavas and Rākṣasas, indeed to all living beings.
t.7.16.10: His eyes red with rage, he descended from the Puṣpaka and, saying, "Who is this Śaṃkara?", went to the foot of the mountain.
t.7.16.11: Then he saw the lord Nandīśvara standing not far off, leaning upon a blazing trident, like a second Śaṃkara.
t.7.16.12: Seeing that monkey-faced one and holding him in contempt, the rākṣasa, out of folly, let loose a roar of laughter, like a cloud laden with water.
t.7.16.13: Then the blessed Nandī, the other body of Śaṃkara, greatly enraged, spoke there to the rākṣasa Daśagrīva, who stood before him.
t.7.16.14: Since, O evil-minded rākṣasa, seeing me in the form of a monkey, you scorn me out of folly and burst into mocking laughter,
t.7.16.15: Therefore monkeys endowed with my form, whose energy equals my own prowess, will indeed be born for the destruction of your race.
t.7.16.17: Then that night-roamer, paying no heed to the words of Nandin, approached that mountain and spoke these words.
t.7.16.16: But what can I do to you now, O night-wanderer? You need not be slain by me, for you have already been slain by your own deeds.
t.7.16.18: Since on account of this the course of the Puṣpaka was cut short while I was travelling, I shall therefore tear up this mountain of yours by its roots, O lord of cattle.
t.7.16.20: Having spoken thus, O king, he then thrust his arms beneath the mountain and lifted up that peak together with its deer, its beasts of prey and its trees.
t.7.16.19: By what power does Bhava sport there like a king? You do not know what ought to be known: a cause for fear has now arrived.
t.7.16.22: Then his arms, which had gone beneath that mountain, were crushed, and the ministers of that Rākṣasa there were struck with amazement.
t.7.16.21: Then, O Rāma, Mahādeva, laughing as he saw what Rāvaṇa had done, playfully pressed down that mountain with his big toe.
t.7.16.23: Out of rage, and from the crushing of his arms, that Rākṣasa let out a tremendous cry, by which the three worlds were filled.
t.7.16.24: Men, terrified by the sound, thought it was the destruction of the world; and even the deities, deeply agitated, were shaken from their own duties.
t.7.16.25: Then Mahādeva, pleased, standing at that time on the summit of the mountain, released his arms, O king, and spoke these words to Daśānana.
t.7.16.27: Since these three worlds have been made to cry out and have been seized by fear, you shall therefore be known as Rāvaṇa; by that name you shall be called.
t.7.16.26: I am pleased with your valor and your heroism, O night-wanderer. From your roaring, released in agony, came forth a cry exceedingly dreadful.
t.7.16.28: Gods, humans, Yakṣas, and all others who dwell upon the face of the earth will thus call you Rāvaṇa, the one who makes the worlds cry out.
t.7.16.29: Go without fear, Paulastya, by whatever path you wish. You have my leave, lord of the rākṣasas; depart.
t.7.16.30: Thus named by Maheśvara himself, Rāvaṇa saluted Mahādeva and ascended that aerial chariot.
t.7.16.31: Then, O Rāma, Rāvaṇa roamed over the surface of the earth, harassing here and there the Kṣatriyas of exceedingly great valour.
